I use static stretches after the run (dynamic stretching in the warmup). Then I will stretch again at night and use he foam roller at night (I run in the morning). The Asian Partnership talks were not as succesfful in creating an alliance as was originally hoped, however it was still fruitful in improving Indian-Pakistan relations. Although India declined membership status (instead deciding to take part with observer status), it has also agreed to respect the de facto territorial claims to the Kasmir region for Pakistan and India respectively.

India and Pakistan have also agreed to setup a 15-mile wide demilitarized zone along their borders running through the Kasmir region. This new DMZ is set to expire on January 21, 2020. The hope here is that relations between India and Pakistan will improve enough by the time the DMZ expires that its existence as a necessity would be irrelevant anyways. Currently this move seems to be getting off to a good start. There are confirming reports that India and Pakistan have both been pulling troops away from the border.

Pakistan also made promise during the APP talks that it would not support rebel factions in the Kasmir region. Some political scholars however have also raised concern that Pakistan followed up this promise by stating that it won't take responsibility for the actions of individuals. Bernd Beber of NYU was quoted as saying that he feels Pakistan should also take steps to actually preventing such attacks from occurring in the future, otherwise the likelihood of improving relations could be jeopardized by chance. Time will tell on this one, but the international community is hoping for the two countries to improve their relations for the long-term.
